questions.enonce_markdown:
Give evidence of the demonstration of God's presence and power in the life of Paul during his trip to Rome.

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** After appealing to Caesar (Acts 25:11), Paul was sent to Rome as a prisoner under the centurion Julius (27:1). Luke's account of the journey, in Acts 27-28, shows God's presence and power in Paul's life in several ways.

**1. Guidance in the storm.** At Fair Havens Paul warned that the voyage would be dangerous (27:9-10), but the officers sailed on and a violent northeaster drove the ship for days. During the storm an angel of God stood by Paul and said, "Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before the emperor; and God has granted safety to all those who are sailing with you" (27:23-24). Paul's confidence came from God.

**2. Leadership and encouragement.** Paul encouraged the crew and passengers to take courage, told them to eat and, in front of everyone, took bread, gave thanks to God and ate (27:33-36). He acted as a prisoner who is strong in faith.

**3. Deliverance in the shipwreck.** The ship ran aground and broke up, but, as the angel had promised, all on board reached land safely, 276 persons in all (27:37, 44). The soldiers' plan to kill the prisoners was stopped by the centurion, who wanted to save Paul (27:42-43).

**4. Protection on Malta.** A viper fastened on Paul's hand, but he shook it off into the fire and suffered no harm (28:3-6). The islanders, who expected him to die, said he was a god, showing how they were impressed.

**5. Healing power.** Paul prayed and laid hands on the father of Publius, the chief man of the island, who was sick with fever and dysentery, and healed him; the other sick on the island came and were cured (28:7-9). The people honoured them and provided for their needs.

**6. Encouragement from the believers at Rome.** When brothers from Rome met Paul at the Forum of Appius and Three Taverns, "he thanked God and took courage" (28:15).

**7. Preaching in Rome.** Under guard, Paul welcomed all who came and proclaimed the kingdom of God "with all boldness and without hindrance" (28:30-31).

**Conclusion.** Luke shows that God keeps his promise to bring Paul to Rome; the journey displays God's presence in danger, in healing and in the continuing witness to the gospel.
